assetPatternBudgets._comment: Browser ExcelJS is served as a runtime asset instead of a duplicated Vite chunk. This ceiling keeps the measured ~948 KB asset near the warning band so payload drift stays visible without blocking the current release.

startupChunkBudgets.label: firebase-core
startupChunkBudgets._comment: Raised from 320000 to 350000. The chunk sat at 91% of the older ceiling with Firebase SDK 12; minor Firebase patch releases were landing on the edge of the budget. Upstream-controlled size, so give explicit headroom. Revisit if utilization exceeds 93%.

startupChunkBudgets.label: app-authenticated-shell
startupChunkBudgets._comment: PR #330: +6000 bytes (1%) for the daily UPC policy, persistence schema and email gate in the authenticated runtime. Comparable CI builds: main beb6ecb = 583.6 KiB; PR df1c36a = 586.6 KiB. Small margin also covers local build configuration variation; severity remains error and near-limit warnings remain enabled.

chunkPatternBudgets._comment: Kept in sync with the firebase-core startup budget above.
PDF.js worker/runtime remains async, but this protects the large PDF viewer chunk from silently drifting toward the global chunk limit.
PDF.js text/import runtime is async and must stay out of the PWA precache. This dedicated budget keeps PDF.js drift visible separately from app-level PDF chunks.
PDF.js worker is a large async runtime asset excluded from install-time precache. Keep it governed separately so worker drift is visible without misclassifying it under the generic JS chunk ceiling.
PDF vendor chunks are async but among the largest payloads; keep a dedicated ceiling so PDF library drift stays visible before it reaches the global chunk budget.

HEIC/HEIF conversion is loaded only for high-efficiency mobile prescription photos and kept out of the PWA precache. A dedicated ceiling preserves release visibility without relaxing the global chunk budget.
